target_name: Liquid Claim Plus Earning Power Cheapness
rationale: The valuation leg adds an annual flow (3-yr average cash earnings) to a balance-sheet stock (act − lt) with an arbitrary implicit capitalization weight of 1x, and since the stock term is typically an order of magnitude larger and drives the cross-sectional dispersion, the signal is likely a near-duplicate of the archived "Net Liquid Claim Cheapness With Gross Profit" (identical quality leg, fmb 3.77 / alpha 2.2%) rather than a genuine test of whether the quality screen repaired the obligation-netted slope.

This is a denominator swap (at → lt) on the quality leg of an already-archived signal, and worse, it re-introduces 1/lt into a signal whose valuation leg already nets lt, so the two legs become mechanically correlated and the "profit per dollar of obligation" leg largely proxies low leverage — a screen the archive has tested repeatedly.

target_name: Liquid Claim That Is Actually Distributed
rationale: Payout as verification that a liquid balance sheet is actually accessible to outside shareholders is a genuine free-cash-flow agency channel untested in the archive and not merely a restatement of dividend yield, though the reviewer should watch for a large tied mass of zero-dividend firms compressing the quality leg and for confounding with size/maturity.

target_name: Rich Price Funding Illiquid Asset Build
rationale: The quality leg is growth in non-current assets, which is essentially the published asset-growth anomaly (Cooper–Gulen–Schill) whose documented concentration among richly priced firms makes the interaction a rediscovery rather than a new mechanism, and GROWTH on a base that can be near zero adds instability.

target_name: Liquid Assets To Price With Light Obligations
rationale: The stated hypothesis is a diagnostic decomposition ("which component drives the alpha") rather than an economic mechanism, and the resulting construct is simply cheap-on-current-assets times low-leverage — a standard and much-studied value×leverage tilt that closely overlaps the archived ceq/mktcap × act/at signal.

target_name: Liquid Claim Tested Through The Cycle
rationale: The through-cycle minimum is a legitimately novel durability concept, but TS_MIN((act−lt)/at,5) is highly correlated with the current (act−lt) that already forms the numerator of the valuation leg, so the product is closer to squaring one balance-sheet quantity than to gating value on an independent quality dimension.
